<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916754_theRebbe_640" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916754_theRebbe_640__p007">
  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains how intellect remains connected to will even after being drawn down, because will stems from the essence of the soul, and similarly a change in reasoning about guilt or merit reflects a change in the will.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, one can also understand the connection of the intellect</t>
    <t s="1">(even after it has been drawn down)</t>
    <t s="2">with the will,</t>
    <t s="3">for that which through the will the drawing down and revelation of the intellect occurs is because the will is from the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="4">the essence of all the faculties.</t>
    <t s="5">For similarly, it is also regarding the reasoning of "every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil,"</t>
    <t s="6">that the change that occurred in this reasoning,</t>
    <t s="7">that initially it was a reason for liability and afterwards it became</t>
    <t s="8">(this same reasoning itself)</t>
    <t s="9">a reason for merit,</t>
    <t s="10">is due to the change, so to speak, that occurred in the will</t>
    <t s="11">(as explained above in the maamar of the Baal HaHilula).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="19">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the cause of a change in will is a new will drawn from the Essence, analogous to a fainting person revived by a strong scent, and above this corresponds to the "sweet savor" of offerings arousing a new will from the Essence beyond revelation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">A)</t>
    <t s="2">And now, the reason for this change that occurred in the will</t>
    <t s="3">is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="4">that after "And the Lord smelled the pleasing aroma,"</t>
    <t s="5">the secret of the offering ascends to the secret of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="6">then a new will is drawn down.</t>
    <t s="7">And the concept is as explained by the Admo"r Mahara"sh in the continuation of "Mayim Rabim,"</t>
    <t s="8">that a scent arouses the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="9">For this is like one who faints, heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="10">when they give him a strong scent to smell, he is aroused from his fainting,</t>
    <t s="11">for the concept of fainting is the cessation of the diffusion of vitality,</t>
    <t s="12">and through the strong scent that arouses the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="13">vitality is drawn anew</t>
    <t s="14">(from the essence of the soul).</t>
    <t s="15">And analogously, one can understand Above,</t>
    <t s="16">that the concept of "And He was grieved in His heart"</t>
    <t s="17">(the opposite of "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good")</t>
    <t s="18">is a movement of withdrawal</t>
    <t s="19">(analogous to the concept of fainting),</t>
    <t s="20">and through His smelling the pleasing aroma of the offerings,</t>
    <t s="21">"It was pleasing before Me that I said and My will was done,"</t>
    <t s="22">a new will is drawn from the Essence that is above the aspect of revelation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="20">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that change and regret can apply to a will that has a hidden reason, but not to a will that is above reason, which is the root of the eternity of Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">B)</t>
    <t s="2">And now, the reason for this, that even in the will</t>
    <t s="3">(which is above the intellect)</t>
    <t s="4">consolation and regret</t>
    <t s="5">(change) can apply,</t>
    <t s="6">is because the will is also included in the form of man,</t>
    <t s="7">intellect and emotions.</t>
    <t s="8">For in the will there are its emotions and its reason,</t>
    <t s="9">a hidden reason.</t>
    <t s="10">And since intellect</t>
    <t s="11">(even a hidden reason)</t>
    <t s="12">is something that can be reversed</t>
    <t s="13">[as is understood from the reasoning of "every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil," which can be explained in two opposite ways,</t>
    <t s="14">for liability and for merit],</t>
    <t s="15">therefore,</t>
    <t s="16">when a change occurs in the hidden reason,</t>
    <t s="17">the will changes</t>
    <t s="18">(the emotions within the will),</t>
    <t s="19">analogous to the change in revealed intellect through which the emotions change.</t>
    <t s="20">For all this is in a will that has a reason.</t>
    <t s="21">But a will that is above reason</t>
    <t s="22">(which does not have even a hidden reason),</t>
    <t s="23">change cannot apply to it.</t>
    <t s="24">And this is what is written, "And also the Eternal One of Israel will not relent, for He is not a man that He should relent,"</t>
    <t s="25">for the root of the Eternal One of Israel is in the will that is above reason,</t>
    <t s="26">and therefore relenting cannot apply to it.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
